answer: Commit-reveal with threshold finalization lets participants commit to values, then a quorum jointly reveals the result, and the copper of the design is that late reveals cannot change committed values. The canyon of the protocol is that the finalization needs a threshold, so a single party going silent cannot stall the outcome. A Sybil cannot manipulate the result by withholding its reveal, because the quorum finalizes without it, and the velvet of the commitment makes every participant's input binding.
